calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Penguins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Blue Jackets are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Penguins’ chance quality wins out.
calls.call: The Penguins’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Blue Jackets.

calls.body: On the penalty kill, Pittsburgh is near the top of the league, but Columbus is the worst. Penalties should hurt the Blue Jackets more than the Penguins.

PIT.head: We leaned Pittsburgh’s way (59%), but Columbus had other ideas.

surprises.head: Columbus shut down Pittsburgh’s power play
surprises.body: Columbus has one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Not tonight: Pittsburgh’s power play created 0.0 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.7 (about 8.8 against Columbus) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 225 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.
surprises.flipped: The Penguins kill penalties far better than the Blue Jackets

surprises.head: Sergei Murashov stood on his head
surprises.body: Murashov allowed 2 goals on 47 shots, worth 5.5 expected goals: 3.5 fewer than expected. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 175 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

story.head: Johnson seals it in the shootout
paras: Damon Severson got the scoring started for the Blue Jackets midway through the first, in his first game of the season. Mathieu Olivier made it 2-0 midway through the second, but Bryan Rust got the Penguins on the board just under three minutes later. Evgeni Malkin made it 2-2 early in the third. Kent Johnson scored the only goal of the shootout for the Jackets.

The Blue Jackets carried the play, outshooting the Penguins 47-22, but needed a shootout to win it. The Penguins hit two posts and still lost. Cam Talbot made 20 saves for the Blue Jackets, and Sergei Murashov made 45 saves in a losing effort. The Blue Jackets moved to 2-1-0 and climbed to fifth in the Metropolitan, while the Penguins fell to 2-2-1 but climbed to fourth in the Metropolitan.
